Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Use the data on the table above to calculate:

(i) The mean monthly temperature

(ii) Temperature range

(iii) Annual average rainfall

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Mean monthly temperature.**

$$
\bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum x}{N}=\dfrac{24+24+26+26+28+28+27+26+26+27+26+25}{12}=\dfrac{313}{12}\approx 26.1\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}
$$

**(ii) Temperature range** = highest monthly temperature minus lowest monthly temperature $= 28 - 24 = 4\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (highest in May and June, lowest in January and February).

**(iii) Annual average rainfall.** Total annual rainfall $= 280+180+150+160+200+160+150+180+200+300+660+630 = 3{,}250$ mm. The average monthly rainfall is $\dfrac{3250}{12}\approx 270.8$ mm, that is about 271 mm per month. (The expression "annual average rainfall" is ambiguous: state the annual total, 3,250 mm, and the monthly average, about 271 mm, so that either reading is covered.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Using the value for mean monthly temperature obtained in (a)(i) above, calculate the standard deviation of the mean monthly temperature using the formula:

$$
\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum(\bar{x}-x)^2}{N}}
$$

Where $x$ = monthly temperatures, $\bar{x}$ = mean monthly temperature, $N$ = number of months (12). (8 marks)

(ii) State the significance of your answer obtained in (b)(i). (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i) Standard deviation (8 marks).** Use $\bar{x}=26.08\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (26.1 gives the same final answer).

| Month | $x$ (°C) | $\bar{x}-x$ | $(\bar{x}-x)^2$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| J | 24 | 2.08 | 4.34 |
| F | 24 | 2.08 | 4.34 |
| M | 26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| A | 26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| M | 28 | -1.92 | 3.67 |
| J | 28 | -1.92 | 3.67 |
| J | 27 | -0.92 | 0.84 |
| A | 26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| S | 26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| O | 27 | -0.92 | 0.84 |
| N | 26 | 0.08 | 0.01 |
| D | 25 | 1.08 | 1.17 |
| | | $\sum$ | 18.92 |

$$
\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{18.92}{12}}=\sqrt{1.576}\approx 1.26\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}
$$

**(b)(ii) Significance (3 marks).** The standard deviation measures how widely the monthly values are spread around the mean. A value of only about $1.3\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ is small compared with the mean of $26.1\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$: the monthly temperatures cluster closely around the mean, with little variation from month to month. So the station has a uniformly hot temperature all year round and almost no thermal seasons, which is typical of an equatorial climate; the mean is a reliable, representative value for the year, and the data are consistent (no extreme months).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Calculate the coefficient of variation stated as:

$$
CV=\dfrac{100\times \text{standard deviation}\ (\sigma)}{\text{mean temperature}}
$$

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$
CV=\dfrac{100\times 1.26}{26.1}\approx 4.8\ \%
$$

(Using $\sigma=1.2555$ and $\bar{x}=26.083$ gives $4.81\ \%$.) A coefficient of variation of under 5 % is very low: the temperature varies very little around its mean, so the temperature regime is very stable through the year, which confirms the standard deviation result.

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) How is the rainfall pattern from September to December in South East Asia different from the pattern in Cameroon? (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**South-East Asia (from the table).** Rainfall **rises steadily and sharply** from September to December: 200 mm in September, 300 mm in October and a maximum of 660 mm in November and 630 mm in December. These four months bring about 1,790 mm, more than half (about 55 %) of the annual total of 3,250 mm; November and December are the wettest months of the year, a late-year rainy season linked, for stations of this kind, to the north-east monsoon winds and the southward shift of the rain belt.

**Cameroon.** Over most of the country rainfall **falls** over the same four months. In the south (equatorial climate) September and October belong to the second rainy season, with the October maximum in many places, and then rainfall decreases sharply in November, December being the start of the long dry season. In the west and the Adamawa, rainfall ends in October or November. In the north the rains stop about October and the Harmattan sets in, so November and December are dry.

**Contrast.** In South-East Asia these months are the wettest of the year, whereas in Cameroon they are the end of the rainy season and the beginning of the dry season; the rainfall regimes are almost opposite in phase.
